clue.text: Midway, through summit, you reported new insight

indicators.note: midway through tells us one piece is placed in the middle of the word for summit

parts.note: a summit or peak is the acme

indicators.note: reported means the word you is given as it is spoken, as the letter U

parts.note: the word you, said aloud, sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: A climber halfway up a peak is told they have gained a fresh perspective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' turns 'you' into the letter U, and 'Midway through' puts that U in the middle of ACME (summit), giving ACUME; N for 'new' finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is sharp discernment, the ability to see quickly into a situation.

clue.text: Club's left half gets a goal, right?

indicators.note: the left half of a word is its first half, read from the left, here two of four letters

parts.note: a goal is an aim

explanation.surface: A football club's left-half scores and asks the referee if it counts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left half' sounds like a football position but asks for the first two letters of 'Club', CL.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim is an entitlement or right to something.

clue.text: Larger case needed for spades, perhaps

parts.note: major means larger or greater
a case in law is a suit

explanation.surface: Someone needs a bigger box to carry their gardening spades.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, spades and hearts are the major suits, scoring more than clubs and diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, spades is one of the two higher-ranking suits, an example of the category.

clue.text: Diplomatic Roman confused about union

indicators.note: confused means the letters that follow are muddled into a new order

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Roman diplomat is bewildered by a trade union's demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' scrambles C (about) with UNION.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is the Pope's ambassador, a diplomat representing the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: After Tom's rebuff, I become uncommunicative

indicators.note: a rebuff is a turning back, so the word for Tom is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
taken as written
to turn means to become, as in turning sour

explanation.surface: Snubbed by Tom, the speaker falls silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name but means a tomcat, and 'rebuff' signals the reversal of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturn describes someone reserved and saying little.

clue.text: Brecht's inexpensive musical production

parts.note: the cheapness hint is a playful description of the title of Brecht and Weill's famous stage work, whose name contains an old small coin

explanation.surface: A Brecht musical staged on a shoestring budget.
explanation.walkthrough: The title includes the name of an old British coin worth three pennies, hence 'inexpensive'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brecht and Weill work of 1928 is named after a coin of tiny value, matching the cheapness joke.

clue.text: Conservative MP again involved in electioneering

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tory member of parliament is once again busy canvassing for votes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles C with MPAGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign is an organised drive, here the canvassing done before an election.

clue.text: In which senators appeared to speak boastfully

parts.note: taken as written
to gas is to talk idly or boastfully

explanation.surface: Roman senators showed up only to brag.
explanation.walkthrough: Senators of ancient Rome appeared in togas, the draped robes of a citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the formal robe worn by Roman senators in public.

clue.text: First-rate sportsman put in the shade

parts.note: royal can mean splendid or first-rate
a Blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University

explanation.surface: A top athlete is outshone by a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: A BLUE is a British university sporting honour, chiefly at Oxford and Cambridge, and the person who wins it.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep vivid colour, a particular hue.

clue.text: Criticize judge and peculiar jack-in-office

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticize it harshly
taken as written
rum is British slang for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a judge and an odd self-important official.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM as 'strange' is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A panjandrum is a pompous official who acts with self-important authority, a petty bureaucrat.

clue.text: Artist finishes off painting too quickly, begorra!

indicators.note: finishes off asks for the final letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: An Irish onlooker exclaims that a picture was dashed off too fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishes off' takes the last letters of painting, too, quickly and begorra.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was a celebrated Spanish painter.

clue.text: Write off to join on the first of April

indicators.note: on means the word for join is placed on, following, the letter taken from April
the first of picks out the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: to mortise is to join timber with a mortise-and-tenon joint

explanation.surface: Someone is told to write off their debts by joining up on April 1st.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letter of April, A, comes before MORTISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To amortise is to reduce a debt or asset value gradually, writing it off over time.

clue.text: Saint spotting another in a tree

indicators.note: in means one piece is set inside the phrase for a tree

parts.note: a tree can be an elm, with the article written as an before it
another saint gives a second S, the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A saint sees a fellow saint up in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a tree' is AN ELM, the article included; 'another' (saint) is S, set in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anselm was an eleventh-century Archbishop of Canterbury, canonised as a saint.

clue.text: Hungry hunter tucked into delectable sausages

indicators.note: tucked into means the name is concealed inside the run of letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A ravenous hunter wolfs down some tasty bangers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' reads as eating but marks the letters inside 'delectablE SAUsages'. In Genesis, Esau the hunter came home famished and sold his birthright for stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau, the Biblical hunter, was so famished he traded his birthright for a meal.

clue.text: One might provide note on legal contents of form

parts.note: so (or soh) is a note of the sol-fa scale
licit means lawful or legal

indicators.note: contents of asks for the inside letters of the next word, without its first and last

explanation.surface: A lawyer drafts a note about the legal details on an official form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents of form' is OR, the middle of fORm. 'One might provide' points to a person who supplies legal services.
explanation.definitionFit: A solicitor is a person, a lawyer who provides legal advice to clients.

clue.text: Outer protection breached before soldiers can go in

definitions.text: Outer protection breached before soldiers can go in

parts.words: Outer protection breached before soldiers can go in
parts.note: reads as a military assault, but describes cracking open a boiled egg before dipping toast fingers into it

explanation.surface: Defences must be broken before the troops can enter.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLDIERS in Britain are strips of toast dipped in a soft-boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin casing of an egg is cracked so toast strips can be dunked in.

clue.text: Treasures from the past, including many in museum

indicators.note: including means the word for treasures from the past holds another piece inside it

parts.note: heritage is what is inherited from the past, valued buildings and objects
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: A museum displays many historic treasures.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hermitage in St Petersburg is one of the world's great museums.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hermitage in St Petersburg is a famous art gallery and museum.

clue.text: Like a cat that's stirred itself up?

indicators.note: stirred means the letters are mixed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cat has worked itself into a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred' scrambles ITSELFUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Catty means malicious, so to be like a cat is to be nasty and vindictive.

clue.text: Even a car ride can produce a state of confusion

parts.note: flat means level or even
a spin is a short drive in a car

explanation.surface: Even a short drive can leave someone flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: A FLAT SPIN was originally an aircraft's uncontrolled spiral, hence panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a flat spin is idiomatic for being agitated or panicked.

clue.text: Regretted making abusive pronouncement

indicators.note: pronouncement means a word is given as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: abusive language is rude

explanation.surface: Someone was sorry for making an insulting statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronouncement' looks like a statement but marks a soundalike of RUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have rued something is to have been sorry for it.

clue.text: Motorway configuration almost leading to accident

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a configuration is a shape

explanation.surface: A badly designed motorway layout almost causes a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 runs from London to Leeds; crosswords write it MI. 'almost' trims SHAPE to SHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky accident.

clue.text: Absolve Parisian who's been taken in by pretence

indicators.note: been taken in by means one piece is held inside the word for pretence

parts.note: an act is a pretence, as in putting on an act
qui is French for who

explanation.surface: A Frenchman fooled by a sham is cleared of blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'been taken in by' suggests being fooled by a sham; it is the container signal, with the French word set inside the pretence.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquit is to declare someone not guilty, clearing them of a charge.

clue.text: Demoralize a peacekeeper

definitions.meaning: a United Nations man, a member of a UN force

explanation.definitionFit: Unman means sap of nerve; read as two parts it names a soldier serving with the United Nations.

clue.text: First novel

explanation.definitionFit: Original means existing from the beginning and also new or inventive.

clue.text: In van, a part of the engine

parts.note: the cylinder head is a part of an engine

explanation.surface: A component found in a delivery van's engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' is short for vanguard, the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the van is to be at the front, leading.

clue.text: Encountered one on the way back also

indicators.note: on the way back means the whole phrase is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: met means encountered
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone bumped into a person while returning home too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' turns the whole of METI round.
explanation.definitionFit: Item is Latin for likewise, used to introduce a further point in a list.

clue.text: What's seen wriggling in clear river? This sort of fish

indicators.note: in means the scrambled piece goes inside the word for clear

parts.note: free can mean clear, as in free of obstruction

indicators.note: wriggling means the letters squirm into a new order

parts.note: here the word and its s are both used as letters

explanation.surface: Something squirming in a clear stream turns out to be a trout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wriggling' scrambles WHATS to SHWAT, which goes 'in' FREE, then R.
explanation.definitionFit: Some fish live only in rivers and lakes rather than the sea.

clue.text: Trim all round fabric

parts.note: to prune is to trim

indicators.note: round means the word all is turned about, read backwards

explanation.surface: Cut the material all the way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like part of trimming all round an edge, but it signals that 'all' is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Prunella is a strong worsted cloth, once used for clergy gowns and shoe uppers.

clue.text: Pretentious upstart posed in absurd fashion

indicators.note: in absurd fashion means the letters are rearranged in a ridiculous way

parts.note: read as up-start, the start of up is the letter U
taken as written

explanation.surface: A social climber struck a ridiculous pose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstart' reads as a social climber but gives U, the start of 'up'; 'in absurd fashion' scrambles U with POSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseudo means sham or affected, giving a false impression of depth.
